backward_compat_traps.i3c: I3C Slaves shall NOT clock-stretch SCL; only the Master may stall.
backward_compat_traps.trap: An I2C slave that retains its clock-stretch behavior cannot operate on an I3C bus; Master will treat held SCL as a bus error.

backward_compat_traps.i2c: 9th SCL bit on data byte = ACK / NACK from receiver.
backward_compat_traps.i3c: 9th SCL bit on data byte = T-Bit (Master odd parity / Slave end-of-data); NO ACK on data.
backward_compat_traps.trap: I2C-firmware ported to I3C must NOT drive ACK on data; doing so corrupts Push-Pull SDA and may damage drivers.

backward_compat_traps.i3c: Mandatory — every I3C slave shall ACK 7'h7E + W.
backward_compat_traps.trap: I2C-style slaves ignoring 7'h7E will miss every Broadcast CCC including ENTDAA — they cannot get a Dynamic Address.

backward_compat_traps.i2c: All transitions are Open-Drain; brief overlap is harmless.
backward_compat_traps.i3c: Address-ACK → Master-Write data requires Open-Drain → Push-Pull handoff with overlap window (Section 5.1.2.3.1) to prevent driver contention.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Incorrect handoff causes shorting of Push-Pull driver against Slave Open-Drain → potential damage.
Long traces / many devices that worked on I2C may be electrically infeasible at I3C SDR speeds.

backward_compat_traps.rule: On Mixed Fast Bus, every I2C device must have a true 50 ns Spike Filter on SCL; otherwise the bus drops to Mixed Slow/Limited speeds.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Adding one I2C device without a Spike Filter caps the entire bus to Fm/Fm+ speeds.

backward_compat_traps.rule: Dynamic Addresses cannot use 7'h00, 7'h01, 7'h02, 7'h3E, 7'h5E, 7'h6E, 7'h76, 7'h7A, 7'h7C, 7'h7E, 7'h7F; several conditional addresses depend on whether legacy I2C devices with extended-address / device-ID modes are present.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Static I2C addresses that fall into these slots are illegal on an I3C bus.

fields.spec_version: Version 1.0 (19 July 2018) — MIPI Board Adopted 8 October 2018

key_changes.summary: Fast-mode (400 kbit/s) added; legacy fixed input levels (1.5/3.0 V) supplemented by 30%/70% VDD spec.
Fast-mode Plus (1 Mbit/s) introduced; Cb up to 550 pF allowed for Fm+.
Ultra Fast-mode (UFm) added — unidirectional, push-pull, 5 Mbit/s; no arbitration.
Editorial cleanup; clarified bus-clear procedure and Device ID read sequence.

fields.version_naming_history_note: MIPI I3C Basic v1.0 is the first public royalty-free release of an MIPI I3C-class specification. The IPR terms (RAND-Z, Annex E) allow non-MIPI-members to implement and license the spec without joining MIPI Alliance, in exchange for reciprocal licensing commitments.
predecessor_protocols: I2C v3.0 (2007) — Fast-mode Plus 1 Mbit/s, 10-bit addressing
I2C Rev. 4 (2012) — Ultra Fast-mode push-pull unidirectional 5 Mbit/s
I2C Rev. 6 (4 April 2014, NXP UM10204) — most recent I2C spec, basis for I3C backward compatibility
i3c_family_versions: MIPI I3C v1.0 (31 December 2016) — full I3C spec, members-only, includes HDR-DDR / HDR-TSP / HDR-TSL / Timing Control
MIPI I3C Basic v1.0 (19 July 2018; Board Adopted 8 October 2018) — royalty-free subset of I3C v1.0 with selected I3C v1.1 features; THIS SPEC
MIPI I3C v1.1 (forthcoming at time of I3C Basic v1.0 release) — full I3C members-only update; Direct R/W CCCs, GETMXDS refinement, SETAASA CCC, low-voltage / high-Cb IO
i3c_v1_0_functions_not_in_basic: Timing Control (Section 5.1.8 of full I3C v1.0)
HDR Double Data Rate Mode (HDR-DDR) — Section 5.2.2
HDR Ternary Modes (HDR-TSP and HDR-TSL) — Section 5.2.3
i3c_v1_1_functions_included_in_basic: Low Voltage / High Capacitive Load IO (Section 6, Table 55)

key_changes_vs_i2c.summary: Push-Pull SCL up to 12.5 MHz (vs 1 MHz Open-Drain); 9-bit data word uses T-Bit (parity / end-of-data) instead of ACK; mandatory 7'h7E broadcast support; Dynamic Address Assignment instead of static; In-Band Interrupt + Hot-Join + Secondary Master mechanisms; tighter Cb ≤ 50 pF.

key_changes_vs_i2c.version: I3C Basic vs full I3C v1.0
key_changes_vs_i2c.summary: HDR modes removed (exit pattern detection retained); Timing Control removed; SETAASA + GETMXDS refinement + low-voltage IO + Direct R/W CCCs added from I3C v1.1.
